text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- A group of 52 academicians wrote an open letter calling for withdrawal of police from the streets and for recognition of November 17, 1996 local election results.

- U.S. congressmen delegation will make short stop-over in Belgrade Friday on way to Montenegro. It is to meet government and opposition officials in Belgrade with the aim of promoting democratic process in Serbia.
- Serbian Supreme court upholds opposition victory in town of Vrsac.
- Group of Montenegrin university professors urges measures be taken to remove Montenegro from Belgrade's tutorship.

- If current situation is not resolved peacefully through negotiations, protests could turn into big social upheaval, says president of the Serbian confederation of independent trade unions Tomislav Banovic.
- Mandate of current Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic is running out, says commentary.
- Vojvodina farmers to meet Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to discuss outstanding payment for their commmodities.

- Destabilisation of dinar exchange rate at beginning of this year is temporary and was caused by non economic factors and unfounded inflationary expectations, says Serbian government central coordination team.

- Value of the German mark will drop below four dinars on black market in a few days, says Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic in reaction to last week's abrupt hike of the German currency against the dinar.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav government and Borad of directors of the Yugoslav National bank will hold meetings Friday on measures to remove consequences of the disparity in the official and the so-called black market foreign exchange rate.
- Yugoslav Assistant Foreign Minister Zivadin Jovanovic received on Thursday Paul Poudade of the French Foreign Ministry who is on a two-day visit to Belgrade.

- Banks say they can sell foreign currency to citizens only when they receive it from central bank, in response to announcement that citizens can buy 1,000 German marks at the official exchange rate (3.3 dinars per one mark).
- State-owned stores have still not changed prices to adapt to holiday drop of the dinar value, they are waiting for producers to make the first move.
- Zivorad Smiljanic elected as new president of the assembly of Province of Vojvodina and Bosko Perosevic re-elected president of the provincial government.
- Belgrade students continued protest during the night.
- Yugoslav United Left (JUL) filed libel suit against the daily Dnevni Telegraf for accusing its secretary of planting a bomb explosion in JUL headquarters.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Black market exchange rate will shortly be stabilised, say experts of the Institute of Economic Sciences.
- Serbian government statement saying the opposition coalition Zajedno won in the town of Nis is beginning of the denoument of the country's two-month drama, says commentary.
